_readme: Hand-entered inputs to the Hormuz Crisis Index. Humans write this file; no script does.
WEEKLY UPDATE: for each component below, set 'value', 'as_of' and 'source'.
Then run:  python update_data.py
value   - the figure, in this block's 'unit'. null = nothing to publish.
as_of   - ISO date the figure was OBSERVED or QUOTED. Not the date you typed it.
Leave it alone if the figure has not changed; the component will
correctly show as stale rather than pretending to be fresh.
source  - who published it, e.g. 'Marsh (Marcus Baker)'. Shown in the public API.
note    - free text: caveats, ranges, anything the number alone does not say.
Appended verbatim to the generated provenance note.
This file holds only the CURRENT figure. History accumulates by itself in
hormuz_history.json weeks[], which the updater appends to on every run.
Read-only fields kept here for context when editing - label, unit, baseline,
primary_source - are cross-checked against app/indices/hormuz.py on every run.
Changing one here without changing it there is reported as an error.
confidence            - 'observed', 'estimate' or 'reconstructed'. How THIS figure
was arrived at.
history_reconstructed - true if the weekly series behind this component was
re-anchored during the 2026-07-26 revision rather than
measured week by week. Drives 'reconstructed_series' in
the API. Set false once a real weekly series exists.
role                  - 'primary' (this file is the source) or 'fallback' (a live
feed is the source; this is only used when it goes dark).
cadence_days          - how old the figure may get before it is reported overdue.
plausible_range       - typo guard. A value outside it aborts the update run.

war_risk.label: War-Risk Insurance (per transit)
war_risk.source: Marsh (Marcus Baker, global head of marine)
war_risk.note: Low end of the 7.5-10% of hull range quoted for Hormuz transits

ship_traffic.label: Hormuz Transits (all commercial vessels)
ship_traffic.note: 15 vessels/day x 7, published 2026-07-19. Used only if the PortWatch feed is unreachable
